verdict.rationale: OpenClaw's docs describe Automations as a built-in scheduler that persists jobs, wakes the agent at the right time, and delivers output to a chat channel, a webhook, or nowhere. The docs live under a cron-jobs page covering scheduled jobs, which points to recurring rather than one-off scheduling. A community user independently reports running agents that schedule tasks. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of recurrence syntax or cron expressions, job management details (listing, editing, pausing), and hands-on evidence that recurring runs are reliable.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can schedule recurring jobs or workflows

citations.quote: Automations are OpenClaw's built-in scheduler. The scheduler persists jobs, wakes the agent at the right time, and can deliver output to a chat channel, a webhook, or nowhere.
Automations: scheduled jobs, webhooks, and Gmail PubSub triggers for the Gateway scheduler
